items.title: Capture Guide
items.text:
Capture Guide is an iPhone app for recording a scene, such as a room or an outdoor area, for 3D Gaussian Splatting (a way of turning photos into a 3D model you can view from any angle). While you walk, the phone trains a rough reconstruction from the frames it has taken so far and marks the places that are still weak. You see those marks in AR and walk there before you leave the scene.

Every capture is also saved as a posed dataset (the photos plus where the camera was for each one), ready for the training software of your choice.

flowchart LR
    A[Walk and capture] --> B[The phone trains a reconstruction]
    B --> C[Guidance shows weak spots]
    C -->|Walk there| A
    A -->|Scene covered| D[Stop and export]

Clip pending: guidance in AR

items.text:

  • Capturing a scene: how to walk through a scene and which frames the app skips.
  • Reading the guidance: what the coloured dots and the yellow camera tell you.
  • Your captures and exporting: looking through captures on the phone, getting them off it and training them.
  • Troubleshooting and FAQ: what to do when tracking is lost or the phone runs hot, and what the error messages mean.

items.title: Capturing a scene
items.text: Capture Guide is built for scenes: rooms and other spaces, indoors or outdoors. It has no mode for small objects.

items.title: Keyframes
items.text:
A 3D reconstruction needs every part of the scene in several photos taken from different places. The app keeps a photo, a keyframe, when your view has changed enough since the last one.

  1. Status pill: counts keyframes. Stops rising when frames blur.
  2. White border: flashes once for each keyframe.
  3. Hand button: turns on manual capture; you take the keyframes.
  • Move between shots: standing still adds nothing.
  • Don't retrace yourself: if you stand close to an earlier keyframe and look the same way, the app skips the frame; from a different direction it counts again.
Details
  • A turn on the spot adds a frame now and then, which keeps the keyframes linked.
  • By default a keyframe is taken when the view shares about 60 % or less with the last one (Matcher in Settings, behind the gear at the bottom right of the camera screen), or after a turn of about 10 degrees.
  • "The same way" means within about 10 degrees. "Close" scales with how far away the surfaces are, from 5 cm up to 30 cm.

items.title: Walking pace and distance
items.text:
Walk slowly and keep the phone steady. Turning fast smears the image, worse in a dim room, and smeared frames are skipped: the count in the pill stops rising until you slow down. If you move too fast for a sharp photo while the app wants one, a yellow tortoise pill "Slow down" replaces the guidance line, with a soft tap. It goes away once a sharp photo is taken. After a fast turn the app may take a slightly softer photo, so the photos stay connected. The app does not enforce a distance to the surfaces; the guidance and the keyframe flashes show whether the phone is picking up your view.

Details
  • A dim room makes the smear worse because the camera exposes longer.
  • The app measures how much each frame smears from the phone's motion sensor. A frame that smears by more than about 3 pixels is skipped. Once the phone has turned about 25 degrees since the last keyframe, up to about 6 pixels is accepted.

items.title: Angles
items.text:
• Look at the same wall or piece of furniture from more than one side.
  • Step sideways rather than only turning.
  • For the floor and ceiling, tilt the phone down or up while you walk.

The guidance shows a yellow camera where to stand and the outlined area to point at, as described in Reading the guidance.

Details
  • A step changes the view of nearby surfaces far more than a turn does, and that change in angle is one of the triggers for a new keyframe.
  • The quality dots and the ring count a turn on the spot as no new direction (Quality dots).

items.title: Light
items.text: Bright, even light gives sharp frames; in dim light turn the lights on or move more slowly. Light that stays the same through the whole capture gives a more even result than light that changes as you go.

items.title: What reconstructs poorly
items.text:
• Mirrors, glass and very shiny surfaces: what they show changes with your viewpoint. Expect weak results there.
  • Moving people or traffic: a reconstruction assumes the scene stands still, so anything that moves can show up as smears. Wait for it to pass when you can.

items.title: Keyframes by hand
items.text:
Turn on manual capture with the hand button on the side rail: the automatic keyframes stop, and while you record, a round shutter button appears above the rail. Tap it to take a keyframe from the next sharp frame. If it flashes red, hold the phone still and try again.

Details

The button flashes red when no sharp frame arrives within about half a second.

items.title: When tracking is lost
items.text:
The app only captures while the phone's tracking (Apple's ARKit) works normally. If tracking drops, for example from fast motion or a scene with too little detail, capture pauses and the phone tries to find its place again.

  1. Status pill: the tracking state.
  2. Relocalising banner: walk back. Counts down to a new segment.
  3. Start new segment here: continue without going back.

To get going again, walk back to where you were: if the phone recognises the place, capture continues in the same segment. Otherwise a new segment starts, and the guidance starts over.

Details
  • A segment is one continuous capture in one coordinate system. The phone starts a new one when it has lost the old coordinate system. Tap "Start new segment here" during the countdown when you do not want to go back.
  • The banner with an orange arrows symbol reads "Relocalising — move back to where you were. Starting a new segment in N s." After 15 seconds without finding the place, capture continues in a new segment.
  • While tracking restarts, the banner reads "Tracking restarting — a new segment starts when tracking returns.", and a second banner with a yellow tortoise reads "Move the phone slowly around to start tracking."
  • Each segment is saved in its own folder.
  • In a new segment the old reconstruction is no longer shown, and the ring around Stop comes back once the segment has its first coverage figure.
  • A capture with more than one segment shows "2 seg" (or more) on its card in your captures, and its Frames tab lists the segments one by one.

items.title: An indoor room
items.text: Walk the room and follow the guidance until it reports "Room covered"; then it has no further target. With LiDAR, grey diagonal hatching marks surfaces the phone sees that the reconstruction does not cover yet, and disappears once you have captured them. Without LiDAR, or with Live splat set to "Off", there is no hatching: use the coloured quality dots (how well each part is covered) and the map instead.

items.title: An outdoor walk
items.text:
Set "Scene" to "Outdoor" in Settings before you tap Record; it can't be changed during a capture. The engine then trains with a sky background and uses larger cells. Moving people and traffic cause the smears described above.

Details

Beyond the range of LiDAR, and on phones without it, the phone estimates depth from the image alone, so distant surfaces still get guidance.

items.title: Keeping the screen on
items.text: The screen does not dim or lock while a capture runs. After you tap Stop, the usual timeout returns once the capture is saved.

items.title: Your captures and exporting
items.text: How to find your captures on the iPhone, get them onto your computer and train one into a 3D Gaussian Splatting model with the free Spirula Studio app.

items.title: Your captures
items.text:
Tap the picture at the bottom left of the camera screen. Your captures appear as cards, newest first.

  1. Close: back to the camera.
  2. Select: pick captures to delete.
  3. Photos: four photos from the capture. Tap to open it.
  4. Name: place and time, or date and time.
  5. Date and place: when and where you captured.
  6. Frames and size: number of keyframes and space on the phone.
  • Rename: open the capture and tap its name at the top.
  • Delete: tap "Select", tap the captures, then "Delete" at the bottom, and confirm. This cannot be undone.
Details
  • A name looks like "Main Street, Lucerne · 16:45".
  • While you select, a check mark appears at the bottom right of each chosen capture.

items.title: Looking at a capture
items.text:
Tap a card to open the capture. Each of its tabs has a section below.

  1. Back: to your captures.
  2. Share: packs the capture into one zip file.
  3. Tabs: Overview, Frames and Splat.
  4. Top view: surfaces and the path you walked, from above.
  5. Map: where you were.
  6. Facts: date, place, frames, segments and size.
  7. Done: back to the camera.
Details

The back button shows a chevron, with the word "Captures" on iOS 18.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
Grey points are the surfaces. A coloured line from a dot to an arrowhead is the path you walked, one colour per segment. Pinch to zoom, drag to move and double-tap to reset.

Details
  • A capture without saved camera positions shows "No top view" instead.
  • A capture without a recorded place has no map.
  • A strip of photos follows the facts.

items.title: Frames
items.text:
The Frames tab lists every keyframe, segment by segment. Here you choose which frames the export leaves out.

  1. Excluded frame: greyed out, with a crossed-out eye.
  2. Frame: tap to see it large.
  1. Tap a frame, then "Exclude" to leave it out of the export, or "Restore" to bring it back.
  2. For several frames, tap "Select", tap the frames, then "Exclude" or "Restore" at the bottom.
Details
  • Nothing is deleted. The photo stays on the phone; only transforms.json, the list of photos that exports read, leaves it out.
  • If the 3D model was built before you excluded frames, a note says that it still contains them.

items.title: Splat
items.text:
If the phone built no model, the tab says why: "Live splat was off", "Built on the Mac" or "No splat yet".

  1. Splat tab: the 3D model the phone built, if there is one.
  2. 3D model: drag to orbit, pinch to zoom.
Details

When more than one segment has a model, a picker above it chooses the segment.

items.title: Where your captures are stored
items.text:
Every capture is saved on the phone while you record, with nothing to switch on. In the Files app, go to On My iPhone, then "Capture Guide". Tap Stop before you leave the app, so the list of photos is complete.

  1. Capture folder: named after the start time in UTC.
  2. capture.json: the name, the place and your excluded frames.
  3. Segment folder: photos and camera positions of one segment.
  4. thumb-v2: the picture on the capture's card.
Details
  • A folder name looks like 2026-10-07T12-30-00Z.
  • overlay-metrics.jsonl is a working file you can ignore. Captures from older versions of the app also have a thumb.jpg, which you can ignore too.
  • There is one folder per segment: segment-0, segment-1 and so on. A segment is one continuous stretch of capture in one coordinate system (Capturing a scene explains when a new one starts).
  • While you capture, the photos are written straight away, but the list in transforms.json is updated after every tenth keyframe and when a segment ends. Stopping updates it too. If the app closes in between, the newest photos stay in images/ but are missing from the list.
  • Sometimes a new segment starts just before Stop. It leaves an empty segment-N folder behind that you can skip.

items.title: Segment folders
items.text:
• images/: the full-resolution photo of every keyframe.
  • transforms.json: where the camera was for each photo, and its lens settings.
  • depth/: the LiDAR depth maps.
  • points.ply: a sparse cloud of coloured points the phone tracked.
  • splat.ply: the 3D model the phone trained while you captured.
Details
  • The photos are stored as the camera sensor records them, turned sideways. The app shows them upright, and training software uses them as they are.
  • Frames you excluded are left out of transforms.json. Once you exclude a frame, transforms.unfiltered.json keeps the full list.
  • depth/ exists in every segment and stays empty without LiDAR.
  • splat.ply (the model is made of many splats) is written after you tap Stop or when a new segment starts. It is there only for captures with Live splat on "This iPhone".
  • overlap_audit.json and wire/ are working files of the app that you can ignore.

items.title: Getting captures off the phone
items.text:
Tap the share button at the top right of an open capture. It packs the capture into one zip file and opens the iOS share sheet. Send it with AirDrop to your Mac, save it to Files, or mail it. Unzipped, the file gives the capture folder with its segment folders, ready for Capture to COLMAP.

  1. Zip file: the capture, without the working copies in wire/.
  2. Apps: send the zip to another app or device.
  3. Save to Files: keeps the zip in the Files app.
Details
  • The share button waits until the capture is saved on the iPhone.
  • A capture can be large, because it holds full-resolution photos.

items.title: Other ways
items.text:
The Capture Guide folder is shared with the Files app. Press and hold a capture folder there to copy it to iCloud Drive or another location. With the phone connected to a Mac by cable, the folder also shows in Finder under the phone's file sharing.

Copy the whole capture folder, or at least the segment folders you want; a segment folder has to stay in one piece, because the photos and transforms.json belong together.

items.title: Choosing a segment
items.text: Each segment has its own coordinate system, so you train each one separately; they cannot be joined into one model. In general, start with the segment that has the most photos.

items.title: Turning a segment into a COLMAP model
items.text: Many 3DGS trainers, Spirula Studio among them, read a COLMAP model: the photos and the camera positions in a standard layout. The Capture to COLMAP app converts a segment folder into one. This is the default route; the quick route skips it.

items.title: Install
items.text:
Capture to COLMAP runs on a Mac with Apple Silicon and macOS 14 or newer.

  1. Download CaptureToColmap-macos-arm64.zip from the latest release and unzip it.
  2. Double-click the app once and click "Done" on the warning that macOS cannot check it for malicious software.
  3. Open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll down to the message that "Capture to COLMAP was blocked", click "Open Anyway" and confirm. From then on it opens normally.
Details
  • The app is not signed, so macOS blocks it at first.
  • A Windows version is planned.

items.title: Converting
items.text:
1. Segment folder: the segment to convert.
  2. Output folder: where the COLMAP model goes.
  3. Options: five dropdowns, each with a recommended entry.
  4. Export: starts the conversion.
  5. Status line: what the app is doing.
  6. Show details: opens the log.
  7. Show in Finder: opens the output folder.
  1. Open Capture to COLMAP.
  2. Next to "Segment folder", click "Choose…" and pick one segment folder, such as segment-0.
  3. "Output folder" is filled in with the same name plus _colmap, next to the segment. Change it with "Choose…" if you like.
  4. Leave "Camera positions", "Photo matching", "Match checking", "Starting points" and "Depth images" on their recommended entries.
  5. Click "Export" and wait. The app shows the elapsed time.
  6. When the status line says "Done", click "Show in Finder".

Photos that the app cannot match well enough are left out of the model. If many are missing, export again with "Match checking" on "Relaxed, checked against the phone's tracking (more photos, slower)".

Details
  • Exporting the same segment again replaces the earlier export.
  • Camera positions: "Refine with the phone's positions (recommended)" matches the photos to each other, starting from where the phone thought the camera was, and keeps the result at real-world scale. "Use the phone's positions as they are" skips that fit.
  • Photo matching: "Neighbouring photos (recommended)" compares each photo with the ones taken around it. "Every photo with every other (slow; short captures only)" compares all of them.
  • Match checking: stays on "Standard (recommended)"; "Relaxed" places more photos and checks them more thoroughly against the phone's positions, which takes longer.
  • Starting points: writes seed.ply, a cloud built from the phone's depth sensor and the phone's own points, together with COLMAP's points, coloured from your photos. Spirula Studio can start training from it.
  • Depth images: "Phone LiDAR" writes the depth sensor's readings next to the photos, which some trainers can use as a guide for the geometry.

items.title: The output folder
items.text:
• images/: copies of the photos, so the folder works on its own and you can move it.
  • sparse/0/: the COLMAP model.
  • seed.ply: the starting points for training.
  • depths/: the phone's depth sensor readings for each photo.
  • work/: the app's working files, which the trainer does not need.
Details
  • seed.ply is absent when Starting points is None or nothing could be built.
  • depths/ is absent when Depth images is None or the capture has no depth sensor data.

items.title: Training
items.text:
Spirula Studio is a free, open-source app that trains a 3D Gaussian Splatting model from your photos, on Macs with Apple Silicon, Windows and Linux. Download it from its releases page. If macOS blocks the first open, use "Open Anyway" as in Install. There are two routes, and both work.

Details

The downloaded Mac build is signed without an Apple developer certificate, which is why macOS may block it.

items.title: Default: through Capture to COLMAP
items.text:
1. Convert the segment with Capture to COLMAP.
  2. Open the output folder, the one with images/ and sparse/0/, in Spirula Studio.
  3. Choose seed.ply from the output folder as the seed point cloud ("Seed point cloud PLY"). This needs Spirula Studio 2026.10.6 or newer; with an older version, skip this step.
  4. To use the depth images, set Spirula Studio's depth supervision weight above 0 (command line: --depth-supervision-weight 0.1).
  5. Start training and watch the preview until it looks good, then save the result as a .ply file and open it in a splat viewer.
Details
  • The conversion refines the camera positions the phone recorded.
  • A long capture can give a seed.ply with more than a million points. You don't need to do anything about it: Spirula Studio's source code shows that it then starts from a random subset as large as its splat limit (one million by default), and in a test on one capture a cloud thinned to 300,000 points trained nearly as well as the full one.
  • At the default depth supervision weight of 0 the depth images are ignored. In our tests they placed surfaces at the measured distance and removed see-through spots in an indoor capture; in an outdoor capture they did not change how the trained scene looked from new viewpoints.

items.title: The quick route: straight from the phone's folder
items.text:
1. Open a segment folder, such as segment-0, directly in Spirula Studio.
  2. Start training and save the result as in the default route.

This route trains on the camera positions as the phone recorded them, without the refinement that Capture to COLMAP does.

Details

Spirula Studio reads the segment's transforms.json and points.ply, so there is no conversion step.

items.title: Other trainers and viewers
items.text:
For the exact buttons, see the Spirula Studio project page. Other 3DGS trainers that read COLMAP also work from the same output folder. To check what the phone built, open its splat.ply in a splat viewer that reads .ply files.

Details

In general, a computer can use more splats and larger images than the phone's engine does, so the result tends to be cleaner than the splat.ply from the phone.

items.title: Getting started
items.text: What you need, how the camera screen is laid out, and your first capture.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• An iPhone with iOS 18 or newer (tested on an iPhone 14 Pro).
  • Optional: a LiDAR sensor, which adds a depth map (a distance for each pixel) to each photo the app keeps and grey hatching over surfaces the reconstruction does not cover yet. The capture works without it.

items.title: Install
items.text:
Coming soon

Capture Guide will be available through TestFlight or the App Store. The links will appear here.

iOS asks for three permissions on first use:

  • Camera: as soon as the app opens, since it starts on the camera.
  • Local network: only used to look for a Mac running the planned companion app.
  • Location: the first time you tap Record, to name a capture after the place and show it on a map; recording starts right away, whatever you answer.

items.title: The camera screen
items.text:
Capture Guide opens on the camera, and nothing is saved until you tap Record. Like the Camera app, the controls stay dark even in Light Mode.

  1. Side rail: one button per guidance layer. White disc means on.
  2. Live splat chip: where the 3D model is built. Tap to change.
  3. Your captures: your newest capture. Tap it to see all.
  4. Record: starts a capture.
  5. Settings: the gear.
Details
  • The chip reads, for example, "Splat: iPhone". The 3D model is made of many splats, tiny blobs of colour.
  • The picture of your newest capture appears after your first capture.

items.title: Your first capture
items.text:
The phone builds the 3D model itself, so you need no other device.

  1. Open Capture Guide and wait while it reads "Preparing splat engine…".
  2. Leave the chip on "Splat: iPhone" and tap Record.
  3. Walk slowly with the camera on the scene and follow the guidance (Capturing a scene, Reading the guidance).
  4. Tap Stop when "Room covered" appears, or when you have everything you want.
  5. When the button at the bottom changes from "Saving splat…" to "Done", tap it. Your captures and exporting shows what you can do with the capture.

  1. Status pill: tracking state and the number of keyframes.
  2. Guidance line: what to do next.
  3. Side rail: guidance layers on and off.
  4. Map button: shows the map again. Tapping the map hides it.
  5. Stop: ends the capture. Its ring fills with coverage.
  6. Settings: some rows are locked while you record.
Details
  • While it prepares, the app tunes its engine for your phone; the camera appears once the engine is ready.
  • A white border flashes once each time the app takes a keyframe, a photo it keeps.
  • The pill reads, for example, "Tracking · 0 frames"; the number counts keyframes.
  • The white ring around Stop appears once the phone has a first coverage figure, and fills as more of the scene is covered.
  • The capture opens when you tap Stop. After saving, the line above "Done" says what was saved, for example "Saved with splat". "Done" takes you back to the camera.
  • The capture stays on the phone. Open it later from the picture at the bottom left, or find it in the Files app.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Open Settings with the gear or the Live splat chip. Rows that change how the camera runs read "Stop to change." during a capture. Some rows explain themselves in a grey second line.

  1. Live splat: where the 3D model is built.
  2. Use LiDAR: on by default; greyed out without the sensor.
  3. Scene: "Indoor" or "Outdoor".
  4. Matcher: what will reconstruct your photos; sets how much a new keyframe shares with the last.
  5. Guidance sounds: a click and a tone for the targets.
  6. Proximity ticks: taps that speed up near the yellow camera.

items.title: Live splat
items.text:
• This iPhone (default).
  • Mac: for the planned Mac companion app, which Capture Guide does not need; pick a Mac found on your network, or type an address.
  • Off: no 3D model and a cooler phone; the guidance still works, without the grey hatching.
Details
  • If the phone cannot start its engine, the chip adds "(unavailable)".
  • If no Mac answers within a few seconds, the capture runs without a 3D model and the chip adds "(not found)".

items.title: Other settings
items.text:
• Scene: "Outdoor" is for scenes that reach far away.
  • Matcher (under Photos): pick the software that will reconstruct your photos. More overlap means more photos.
    • "SIFT (60 %)" is the default and suits Capture to COLMAP, which uses SIFT.
    • "SIFT — more overlap (72 %)" takes more photos, for hard scenes or other photogrammetry software.
    • "ALIKED (35 %)" takes the fewest photos, for software that matches with ALIKED and LightGlue.
    • "Custom" shows a slider from 25 to 85 %.
  • Coverage colours (under Guidance): the colours of the quality dots and the map, "Blue-Orange" by default or "Cividis", which runs from dark blue to yellow.
Details

"Outdoor" trains the model with a sky background and uses larger cells.

items.title: Reading the guidance
items.text:
What the on-screen guidance tells you while you capture, and what to do about each part.

The phone keeps its own map of the surfaces it has seen and how well your photos cover them. With Live splat on "This iPhone", it also trains a rough 3D model as you walk. The first dots and hatching show up a little while after you tap Record, once there is something to judge. With Live splat set to "Off", everything below still works except the grey hatching and the 3D model.

items.title: Overlays in the room
items.text:
1. Guidance line: what to do next.
  2. Yellow camera: where to stand for the next view.
  3. Outlined area: what to point the phone at.
  4. Weak dot: a spot that still needs work.
  5. Floor ring: under the yellow camera, where you stand.
  6. Good dot: a spot your photos already cover well.
  7. Grey hatching: surface the reconstruction has not reached yet.

items.title: Controls
items.text:
1. Splat view: the 3D model instead of the camera image.
  2. Quality dots: the dots on or off.
  3. Hatch: the grey hatching on or off.
  4. Next-view targets: the yellow camera and its area on or off.
  5. Keyframe frustums: the keyframe pyramids on or off.
  6. Manual capture: take keyframes yourself.
  7. Stop: ends the capture; its ring shows coverage.
  8. Minimap: the area around you, seen from above.

items.title: Next-view target
items.text:
The app picks one weak area at a time. Go to the yellow camera and face the outlined area; close to the camera, a ring appears at the area itself. Once you are in position, a keyframe is taken (or you tap the shutter) and the next target follows.

  1. Edge arrow: a white arrowhead pointing to the off-screen yellow camera.
Details
  • You are in position within about 0.5 m of the yellow camera, looking roughly at the area.
  • With automatic keyframes on, the app then takes the keyframe by itself; you feel a tap and hear a click. With manual capture, tap the shutter button yourself.
  • A target ends in one of four ways:
    • A keyframe is taken while you are in position. You hear a tone and feel a tap, "Captured" shows, and the next target follows.
    • Other photos you take cover the area first.
    • You do not approach for about 20 s. The app drops the target and may offer another.
    • Another area becomes clearly more important.
  • No target shows during the first 20 s of a segment.
  • Targets need the "Next-view targets" button on (it is on by default) and a running capture. They pause in the splat view.

items.title: The guidance line
items.text:
The line under the status pill, and under any banners, shows one of these:

  • "Stand at the yellow camera and point it at the outlined area": still far from it.
  • "Point at the outlined area": at the camera, facing elsewhere.
  • "Turn toward the outlined area": the same, arrow shows which way.
  • "Good — hold steady": in position; the target turns green.
  • "Captured": target done; stays a second.
  • "Keep scanning — the next view appears shortly": weak areas left, no target yet.
  • "Room covered", in green: no weak area left.

When "Room covered" shows, you can stop, or carry on if you want a denser capture.

items.title: Guidance sounds and taps
items.text:
A click tells you that you reached the yellow camera, and a tone that its area is covered; you feel a tap each time as well. "Proximity ticks" are soft taps that come faster as you get nearer to the yellow camera, like a parking sensor. The "Guidance sounds" and "Proximity ticks" switches in Settings, under Guidance, turn them off.

Details
  • "Guidance sounds" covers the click and the tone. The taps on arrival and completion do not depend on it.
  • The phone's silent switch mutes the sounds as well, and music or podcasts keep playing underneath.
  • Proximity ticks stop once you are in position.

items.title: Quality dots
items.text:
The dots lie on the surfaces the phone knows. With the default colours, "Blue-Orange", light blue is well covered, the colour darkens as coverage gets worse, and orange needs work. Walk towards the weak dots and look at them from a new side; moving sideways helps more than turning on the spot, as Capturing a scene explains. Walk around a surface rather than along it to fill corners and edges.

Details
  • A spot gets full marks once the phone has seen it from 3 clearly different directions and from close enough at least once. Fewer directions, or only distant photos, leave the dot towards orange.
  • Different directions: at least 25° apart. Standing 2 m from a wall, about 1 m sideways gives a new direction. Turning on the spot gives none.
  • Close enough: within about 2 m with the main camera, about 1 m with the ultra-wide.
  • The colours change as the phone takes new keyframes.
  • "Coverage colours" in Settings switches the colour scheme. The map legend always shows the one you picked, from "good" to "needs work".
  • The guidance keeps working with the dots turned off.

items.title: Grey hatching
items.text:
The grey diagonal stripes lie over a faint grey fill, on surfaces the LiDAR sensor has found. Point the camera at them; they disappear as the reconstruction catches up.

Details
  • Hatched means the reconstruction has nothing within about 10 cm of the surface.
  • Hatching needs LiDAR and a Live splat setting other than "Off".
  • It stays off until the first reconstruction exists.

items.title: Keyframe frustums
items.text:
The colour of each pyramid tells you how well that keyframe is tied to the others, from "needs work" to "good". Where pyramids sit at the "needs work" end, add views in between and around them, so each keyframe shares more of its view with its neighbours.

  1. Keyframe frustum: a keyframe's place, pointing the way the camera looked.
Details
  • The colour is the share of a keyframe's view that another keyframe also sees: "needs work" at 0 %, "good" at the overlap your Matcher sets (60 % by default).
  • A white pyramid means the app cannot judge that keyframe yet.
  • A new segment clears them, because the old coordinate system is gone.
  • They are on by default.

items.title: The side rail
items.text:
The buttons on the right edge are named in the Controls figure. A white disc behind a button means on; a plain white symbol means off.

Details
  • The Splat view button appears once the phone has built part of the 3D model, with Live splat on "This iPhone".
  • The Hatch button appears when the phone uses LiDAR (a phone with the sensor and "Use LiDAR" on in Settings) and Live splat is not "Off".

items.title: Splat view
items.text:
In the splat view the other layers are hidden. Where the model has nothing yet, the screen stays black; gaps and thin areas are places it has not learned. Switch it on for a quick look, then off again to carry on with the guidance.

  1. 3D model: what the phone has built so far.
  2. Splat view button: on; tap again for the camera image.
  3. Manual capture: the only other button left.
  4. Minimap: stays in the splat view.

items.title: Progress ring
items.text:
The filled part of the white ring around Stop is the share of the known surface seen from at least 3 clearly different directions, with at least one photo from close enough. It grows as you fill gaps; the quality dots show which spots still need work. Use it to judge how far along you are. Walk around surfaces and look at them from new sides to fill it.

Details
  • The ring appears a little after you start, once the phone has its first coverage figure.
  • "Different directions" and "close enough" mean the same as for the quality dots.
  • After a quick walk through the room in one pass, the ring often stays well below half.
  • It rarely reaches the full circle: corners you cannot reach and surfaces seen from one side keep it below that.
  • When a new segment starts, the ring disappears until the new segment has its own figure.

items.title: Minimap
items.text:
The round map looks down on the area around you: your view direction points up, and the white triangle in the middle is you. Its squares are coloured like the dots, so it shows weak spots even behind you, and a yellow dot marks the next-view target. Use it to pick where to walk; the target and dots show the details. Tap the map to hide it; a round map button takes its place and brings it back.

Details
  • The map covers 5 m around you. Each small square is a patch of known surface, with the legend "good" and "needs work" under the map.
  • The yellow dot has a short arrow towards the area to point at. If the yellow camera is more than 5 m away, the dot sits on the rim.

items.title: Troubleshooting and FAQ
items.text:
Common problems and what to do about them, plus short answers to the questions people ask first.

The camera screen shows problems as dark banners near the top. The symbol tells you the kind: orange arrows when tracking is lost, a yellow tortoise for a hint, a red octagon for an error.

items.title: Tracking is lost
items.text:
A banner appears under the status pill. The phone lost track of where it is, usually after fast movement or in a scene with little to see, such as a blank wall.

  • Walk back to where you were and hold the camera on something with detail. If the phone recognises the place, capture carries on in the same segment.
  • To carry on from here instead, tap "Start new segment here". Capture continues in a new segment with fresh guidance.
  • Or do nothing: the app starts a new segment by itself when the banner's countdown ends.

Capturing a scene explains segments.

Details
  • The banner reads "Relocalising — move back to where you were. Starting a new segment in N s." with a "Start new segment here" button, or "Tracking restarting — a new segment starts when tracking returns."
  • A second banner may read "Move the phone slowly around to start tracking."
  • The countdown is 15 seconds.

items.title: The result looks warped
items.text:
Walls bend because the camera positions have probably drifted (slid away from the truth) without the app noticing.

  • Keep captures short, with plenty of detail in view (this generally drifts less).

items.title: Keyframes are not being taken
items.text:
The frame count in the status pill stays where it is while you walk. Frames are too blurry, or you are standing still.

  • Walk and turn more slowly. When you move too fast for a sharp photo, a yellow tortoise pill "Slow down" replaces the guidance line, with a soft tap. It goes away once a sharp photo is taken. After a fast turn the app may take a slightly softer photo, so the photos stay connected.
  • Add light.
  • Check the hand button on the side rail. With manual capture on, the app takes keyframes only when you tap the shutter.

Capturing a scene has the details.

Details
  • The pill reads, for example, "Tracking · 12 frames".
  • A dim room makes blur worse, because the camera exposes longer.

items.title: No guidance appears
items.text:
• Wait a little. There is nothing to judge right after you tap Record.
  • Check the side rail: a layer without a white disc behind its button is off.
  • Turn the splat view off. The layers show only while it is off.
  • For the grey hatching, turn "Use LiDAR" on and set Live splat to anything but "Off".

Reading the guidance describes each layer.

Details

The dots, the map and the ring appear a little after you tap Record. Next-view targets wait for 20 seconds after a segment starts.

items.title: The guidance is slow and the phone is hot
items.text:
The dots and targets lag behind what you have just captured, and the phone feels warm. With Live splat on "This iPhone", the phone trains the 3D model while it also tracks, films and draws the guidance.

  • Let the phone cool down in the shade, out of its case, before you go on.
  • Turn the dots off with the "Quality dots" button on the side rail. This saves drawing work.
  • For the next capture, set Live splat to "Off" in Settings (what that changes).
Details

In general, an iPhone that gets hot slows itself down to cool off, so the guidance comes later.

items.title: A red banner starts with "Live splat:"
items.text:
The 3D model has a problem.

  • If the banner stays, tap Stop to save your photos. The line above Done may then read "Saved · no splat".

items.title: The camera stopped
items.text:
A red banner starts with "Camera stopped:".

  • Tap "Restart camera" in the banner.

items.title: "Server and app versions do not match"
items.text:
It shows in a red banner. You chose "Mac" under Live splat, and the Mac companion speaks a different version from the app. Until you update, the app cannot read the guidance from the Mac. Capture and export keep working.

  • Update both the app and the Mac companion so they match.
Details

The message appears when the first guidance update from the Mac arrives in a format the app does not know. With "This iPhone" or "Off" you never see it.

items.title: The export is missing or incomplete
items.text:
A save fails after Stop, a red banner reports an export error, or photos you expect are missing from the capture's folder. The phone could not write the files; in general, the usual cause is a full phone.

  • Free up space on the phone and capture again.
  • Look in Files under On My iPhone, then "Capture Guide", not iCloud Drive.
  • Always tap Stop before you leave the app. Wait until the button reads "Done" if you want the splat.ply too.
  • Photos missing from transforms.json are still in images/. Your captures and exporting explains the folder layout.
Details
  • After Stop, the line above Done may read "Save failed · waiting for the splat", "Save failed · no splat", "Splat saved · photos failed" or "Splat on the Mac · photos failed".
  • During the capture, a red banner may read "Cannot create export folder segment-N: …" or "Export flush failed: …".
  • Closing the app before you tap Stop can leave the newest photos out of transforms.json.
  • "Saved · no splat" on its own means the photos are saved but the 3D model could not be written. The capture is still complete for export.

items.title: Which iPhones does it work on?
items.text: Capture Guide was tested on an iPhone 14 Pro. It needs iOS 18 or newer and a phone that supports ARKit, Apple's augmented reality framework.

items.title: Do I need a LiDAR sensor?
items.text:
No, the app captures without it. LiDAR adds a depth map to each keyframe and makes the grey hatching possible.

Details

On a phone without the sensor, "Use LiDAR" in Settings is greyed out.

items.title: Do I need an internet connection or Wi-Fi?
items.text:
No: with Live splat on "This iPhone" or "Off", the capture runs entirely on the phone. Only the "Mac" option and the place name use a network.

Details
  • The "Mac" option looks for the Mac companion on your local network, which is why iOS asks for that permission. With "Mac" chosen, the keyframes go to that Mac over your network.
  • To name a capture after its place, the app asks Apple's map service for the place name, which sends the capture's coordinates to Apple.
  • Without a connection the capture is named by date and time, and it gets the place name the next time you open it online. Without location access it keeps the date and time.

items.title: Where is my data stored?
items.text: On the phone, in the Capture Guide folder of the Files app. The app sends your photos nowhere by itself; what goes over a network is in the answer above.

items.title: What does Live splat "Off" do?
items.text:
The phone builds no 3D model and stays cooler, but it saves the same photos and still guides you with the dots, the map, the ring and the next-view targets. There is no grey hatching, and you export and train as usual.

Details

The capture's Splat tab says "Live splat was off".

items.title: Is there a Mac app?
items.text: A Mac companion app is planned. Capture Guide does not need it.
